subject.title: [Feature]: Feishu Group Chat SubAgents for User-Specific Skills and Memory

question: Should Feishu group chat isolation be solved by extending sender-scoped session/thread bindings, by automatic per-user group subagents with separate skills/config/memory, or by a plugin experiment first?
rationale: Current main has partial primitives, but the requested behavior adds durable agent lifecycle, per-user memory and skill/config isolation, admin control, and security policy, which automation should not choose without owner direction.

options.title: Design narrow channel/session isolation first
options.body: Use current groupSessionScope and session-binding architecture as the baseline, then add only the missing Feishu or SDK seams after resolving the related threading and multi-bot identity issues.

options.title: Sponsor per-user group subagents
options.body: Accept the proposed architecture and require a design for lifecycle TTL, warm pool or cold start behavior, cost/agent limits, permissions, memory tiers, and migration or doctor behavior before implementation.

options.title: Prove it as a plugin experiment
options.body: Keep OpenClaw core lean by asking for an external Feishu plugin or ClawHub proof and promote only the missing generic SDK hook if current plugin APIs are insufficient.

recommendation.title: Design narrow channel/session isolation first
recommendation.body: Use current groupSessionScope and session-binding architecture as the baseline, then add only the missing Feishu or SDK seams after resolving the related threading and multi-bot identity issues.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the adjacent Feishu ACP/subagent session-binding implementation that any approved design would likely extend or replace.
